options.reply: Maybe so, maybe not. I've run that deal a thousand ways, and I can't see the side of it where he gets a good return.

sebastian_bloodmage.open: Twelve years on the grill at my grandmother's place, boss, forty tables and a wood fire. Ask me anything about meat, I dare you.

options.text: How do you know when it's ready?
options.reply: You listen, che. The fat tells you, the smoke tells you, the smell tells you. I could tell a steak was ready from across the room with my back turned.
Get out of my sight, boss. No, come back, I'm joking, sit, I'll make yours medium and you'll thank me for the rest of your life.
Every day, che. The noise, the fire, Saturday night with every table full. Here I cook for whoever turns up, and that's good too, but it's not the same.

sebastian_bloodmage.open: There was a man, boss, Tomas, a sommelier. He left for a job in Mendoza a year before all this. I blame the wine region, personally.

options.text: Do you still think about him?
options.reply: Sometimes, che, sometimes. It doesn't make me sad any more, it's just a good wine you remember. You don't need the bottle to know it was good.
Ha, exactly, boss, exactly, Mendoza's loss! You're a good man, I'm putting extra on your plate tonight.

options.text: A sommelier and a grill man. That's a dangerous pair.
options.reply: Dangerous for everybody's waistline, che. We fed half of Palermo between us, and argued about every bottle.

sebastian_bloodmage.open: The Forsaken barely eat, boss. That was the hardest thing about landing here, and I'm working on a recipe they can actually taste.

options.reply: Close, che, very close. Strong smoke, a lot of salt, something with a bite. The farmer's neighbour tried it last week and almost smiled.

options.text: Why does it matter so much to you?
options.reply: Because an empty table is the worst thing in the world, boss. If I can get one dead man to sit down and enjoy a plate, then nobody's table is empty.

options.text: Make sure I get a taste first.
options.reply: You'll be the first living mouth on it, che, after me. That's a promise.

sondre_stormbringer.open: I taught sailing on the Hardangerfjord for four summers, to teenagers. Most of what I know about people I learned in a dinghy.

options.reply: That the asking is the part that kills people. You say get down once, clearly, early, and then you trust them to do it. Shouting only frightens them.
Every day, a little. The sea here is the wrong colour, but it moves the same way, and on calm mornings I can almost pretend.

options.text: Teaching teenagers? You're braver than you look.
options.reply: Ha, that is the bravest thing I have ever done, and I have been in a storm I made myself. They are terrifying.

sondre_stormbringer.open: My sister Ingrid is four years younger than me and much braver. My father captains a ferry and my mother is a dentist. They are in Bergen.

options.text: You always talk about them in the present tense.
options.reply: Yes, I do, on purpose, every time. It is like holding a door open with my foot. I am not ready to take my foot away.
Loud, fearless, rude to everyone she loves. She would get on very well with some of you, and she would tease me without mercy.

options.text: Bergen sounds like a good place to be from.
options.reply: It rains nearly every day and nobody minds. That is the best thing I can say about anywhere, I think.

sondre_stormbringer.open: People think I want power, because of what I can do. I do not. I have plenty of power, and that is the whole problem.

options.reply: Control, only that. A whole day without being afraid of my own hands. That is all, and some days it feels like a great deal to ask.

options.text: Practising alone isn't the way, you know.
options.reply: I know, I know. Everyone tells me so, and they are probably right. It is only that alone, the only person I can hurt is me.

options.text: You haven't hurt anyone with us.
options.reply: Not yet, no. Thank you, I think. I will try to hear it as a fact and not as luck.

yiannis_paladin.open: Every soul the sea gives up on this shore, {player}, I am there to pull them out. I was there for the first one, before the elves even had tents.

options.reply: An elf girl, not breathing. I did what we do on the harbour, and while I did it, light came into my hands. She breathed, and I sang her a couplet about it.
Because I was already in the water, re. God does not choose the best man, He chooses the one who is wet already.

options.text: Did you sing for me when I came out?
options.reply: Of course I did, little one, a very good one, about your terrible hair. I will sing it at your wedding.

yiannis_paladin.open: Eleni and the girls, Maria and Katerina, are in Chania. Every night I talk to them on the beach, out loud. I do not care who hears.

options.reply: Everything, my friend. Who came out of the water, what I ate, what foolish thing the young ones did. Tonight I will tell them about you.
The sea carries everything somewhere, re. Maybe not to Chania, but somewhere. That is enough for an old man.
I will, and Eleni will ask if you are eating properly, and I will lie for you.

yiannis_paladin.open: People ask me how I still believe, here, in this strange place. As if the Light in my hands should make me doubt the saint on my wall.

options.reply: No, re, never. A fisherman always knew there was something under the water he could not see. Now I can see a little more of it, that is all.

options.text: Maybe the Light is the saint.
options.reply: Maybe, my friend, maybe. I do not need to know which is which. I just need it to come when the child is not breathing.

options.text: I don't know how you do it.
options.reply: You do not need to know. Sit with me some evening, and watch the sea, and maybe you will feel it a little.

friend.open: Boss, I wanted to say, you're not a customer any more, okay? You're one of my people now, and my people get everything fixed for free.

options.text: Free repairs for life? I'm honoured.
options.reply: For life, my friend, and I mean it. Bring me your broken things and your bad days, both work the same way.

options.text: You're one of mine too, Diego.
options.reply: Ha, okay, now you're going to make me cry on my own boots. Stop it, boss.

sworn.open: I'm going to show you something nobody's seen, boss. Here, this is Senora Chispa. She's the beetle. I want you there when she walks.

options.reply: Good, good, my friend. Then I'll stop being scared of finishing her, because somebody's going to be there.
She is, eh? My mother would've said so too, and then asked why it took me eighteen years.

reconciled.open: So, me and {name}, we talked. Properly, no shouting. I think we're okay now, boss, and I wanted you to hear it from me.

options.reply: Yeah, it is. People are harder to fix than machines, but they stay fixed longer when you do it right.
Ha, I know, I know, we're both stubborn like old bolts. But we got there, my friend.

friend.open: I owe you an explanation for why I ask everyone, {player}. On a Bloodsail ship I took a prisoner's blood to save their captain, and I didn't ask him. He died that night.

options.reply: Every time, of everyone, on the record. It doesn't balance the account, but it's the only payment I can make.

options.text: Thank you for telling me the truth.
options.reply: You're owed it. I won't ask for your consent to my company without telling you what that company has done.

sworn.open: I've told you I'd let you hold the knife, {player}. Now I'd let you tell me to put it down, and I'd listen. That's a great deal more.

options.text: I'll only ever say it if I mean it.
options.reply: I know you will. That's precisely why I'd listen.

options.text: Then we look after each other.
options.reply: Agreed, with full and informed consent on both sides. It's the best contract I've ever entered.

reconciled.open: {name} and I spoke at length, and frankly. We've resolved it, and I wanted you to know it was resolved properly.

options.reply: As am I. An unresolved conflict festers, and I'd rather not have to treat it later.
Meaning we each named what we'd done, and the other agreed to it. Old habits, I'm afraid.

friend.open: I'm going to tell you something, {player}, and I won't tell it twice. My falling partner, Travis. A dead limb came out of a tree I was cutting. That's why I yell about the canopy.

options.reply: That's what everybody said. Took me years to even half believe it. Hearing it from you helps a little.
Yep, I figured it was time. You're the first one out here I've told. Seemed like you ought to know why I'm the way I am.

sworn.open: Up a tree, you only trust one person on the ground to watch the canopy for you, {player}. For a long time nobody. Now it's you.

options.reply: I know you will. That's why I can climb again.

options.text: Then climb, Leif. I've got you.
options.reply: Yep, you always do. Alright, I'm going up.

reconciled.open: Me and {name} hashed it out. Took a while, both of us being stubborn as old growth, but we're good now.

options.reply: Yep, me too. Feels lighter, carrying it around without that.
Old trees grow slow, {player}. We got there.

friend.open: I've never once looked at the lists, {player}, not in three whole years. While I don't look, they're all alive. I wanted to say that out loud to somebody, once.

options.text: When you're ready, I'll come with you to read them.
options.reply: You'd do that, for an old man? Allora, maybe I'll be ready sooner than I thought.

options.text: That's a heavy thing to carry alone.
options.reply: It is, and I'm tired of carrying it. Now you've got a corner of it, and that's lighter already.

sworn.open: In my quarter, a person you'd trust with your door was family, {player}. You are family to me now, and that's not something I say to anyone.

options.text: Then you're family to me too, Marco.
options.reply: Good, it's settled. And family doesn't pay for drinks when I'm at the table, so put that away.
Don't be honoured, be family. It's more work, and it's better.

reconciled.open: {name} and I spoke, properly, like people of sense. It's mended now, and I wanted you to hear it from me.

options.reply: So am I. A crack in a street spreads if nobody fixes it.
Ha, an old man never tells that. But I paid for the drinks, so you can guess.

friend.open: There's something I've never told anybody here, {player}. A flood once took a trailer park my warning had named. People died who didn't need to. That's why I say everything three times.

options.text: You warned them. That's on the people who ignored it.
options.reply: That's what I tell myself at three in the morning. Hearing somebody else say it is different, and I'm grateful.

options.text: Thank you for trusting me with that.
options.reply: You're one of the very few, you know. Probably the only one on this whole world.

sworn.open: My mum told me every Christmas that my job was a waste of a good degree, {player}. The last Christmas, she said it too. I've wanted to tell somebody that for a very long time.

options.reply: I think she might have been, yes. It's strange, hearing myself agree with you on that.

options.text: I'd have loved to meet her anyway.
options.reply: Ha, she'd have liked you. She'd have told you to get a proper job, but she'd have liked you.

reconciled.open: Me and {name} talked it through, properly. Two very stubborn weather systems, but they've merged now, and we're okay. I wanted you to know.

options.reply: It is, isn't it? Clear skies, for once, and I didn't even have to forecast it.
It did, sorry, slow-moving fronts. But we got there in the end.

friend.open: You're one of my boys now, {player}, my front row. That means I'll stand in front of anything for you, no questions.

options.text: Then I'll be right behind you.
options.reply: That's the way, butt. You push, I hold, and nothing gets through us.

options.text: Do I have to learn the songs?
options.reply: Every word, mun, and I'll be testing you in the next tavern.

sworn.open: Here, take this. My podger spanner, from the scaffolds at home. Had it on my wrist the day I came through. I want you to have it.

options.reply: You can, and you will, butt. I've got the fire now, I don't need the spanner to hold things together any more.
I know you will. Check your straps with it, now and then, for me.

reconciled.open: Me and {name} had it out, {player}, properly, over a cuppa. I think we're sorted now, and I wanted you to know first.

options.reply: Too short for grudges, aye. Long enough for tea, though.
Nothing much, butt. We both said sorry at the same time and then laughed like idiots.

friend.open: My grandmother raised me in Cork, {player}, a woman called Nora. The rosary and very strong opinions about right and wrong. I'm glad she didn't live to see Boston, and I've never said her name out loud here.

options.text: She'd see who you are now, too.
options.reply: She would, and she'd still have a word or two to say. But maybe she'd say them more quietly, and that's something.

options.text: Thank you for telling me about her.
options.reply: She'd have taken to you. She liked anyone who'd look you in the eye and tell you the truth, God help them.

sworn.open: I said once I'd sign anything you put in front of me without reading it, {player}. It was a joke at the time. It isn't any more.

options.text: I'd never put anything in front of you I wouldn't sign myself.
options.reply: I know you wouldn't. That's why it's the most dangerous thing I've ever meant.

options.text: Then don't read it. I've got you.
options.reply: Grand, then, I won't. No small print, for the first time in my life.

reconciled.open: {name} and I sorted it, properly, no small print. I wanted you to hear it from me before you heard it from the rumour mill.

options.reply: Ah, a gentleman never says. But I bought the round, so draw your own conclusions.
So am I, which surprises me more than anyone. Fair terms all round.

friend.open: Boss, you've got a chair at my table now. Not a guest chair, a family chair. That means you never pay and you never leave hungry.

options.reply: Good, che, because it wasn't really a question. Sit, sit, the meat's nearly ready.

options.text: Do I get to sit next to you?
options.reply: Next to me? Boss, I don't sit. But you get the chair beside where I'd sit, and that's the best one.

sworn.open: Here, boss, take this. My grandmother's chimichurri, the card, in her handwriting. I want somebody else to know it, in case.

options.text: I'll keep it safe. And I'll learn it.
options.reply: Learn it properly, che, the garlic fine, never in a machine. Then one day you cook it for me, and I sit down.
In case I forget how it tasted, boss. That's my real fear, more than dying. Now two of us will remember.

reconciled.open: Me and {name}, we sat down together, boss. Ate, talked, no shouting. I think we're good now, and I wanted you to know.

options.reply: Almost everything, che. Food and time and somebody willing to pass the bread first.

options.text: I'm glad. You both needed it.
options.reply: We did, boss. Life's too short to eat angry.

friend.open: I would like you to stand beside me when the weather turns, from now on, not behind. I do not ask that of many people.

options.reply: Thank you, truly. Then I will try very hard to be worth standing beside.

options.text: Are you sure? I've seen what you can do.
options.reply: That is exactly why I am asking you, and not someone who has not seen it.

sworn.open: This is my shackle key, from the boats at home. I have worn it every day for six years now. I would like you to hold it for a while.

options.reply: I know you will. That is why it is you, and not anyone else.
Because when I hold it I am afraid, and I want to try being without it, near someone I trust.

reconciled.open: {name} and I talked, properly, without anyone shouting. I think we are all right now, and I wanted you to hear it from me first.

options.reply: So am I. It is easier to stand near someone when you are not at odds with them.
Nothing very much, I think. We were both a little wrong and a little stubborn, and we got tired of it.

friend.open: You are family now, {player}, and in Crete that means you eat at my table forever, and I worry about you forever.

options.reply: Good, because you were going to get both anyway. Sit, eat, let me worry.
Especially then, re. Distance is when an old man worries the most.

sworn.open: This is for you, my friend. A little icon of Saint Nicholas, patron of sailors. He kept me on the water forty years. Now he keeps you.

options.reply: You are not taking him, I am sending him with you. He has been on the beach long enough, he wants to travel.
Keep him in your pocket, near your heart, and when the water gets rough, talk to him. He listens better than me.

reconciled.open: {name} and I broke bread together, {player}, and talked like men. I think the storm has passed between us, and I wanted you to know.

options.reply: Bread and time and an old man who finally keeps his mouth closed long enough to listen.
So am I, re. The sea is too big to share it with an enemy.

arguments.third: Diego builds his own grill, and you two have a cook-off in the next town.
lines: diego_tinker
Listen, listen, if I put a little spring bellows under your grill, my friend, the coals stay perfect all night without you touching them!
sebastian_bloodmage
Without touching them? Che, the touching is the whole point, the fire tells you things with your hands in it.
diego_tinker
Sure, sure, and my bellows tells you things without burning your hair off. Your eyebrows are half gone, look at them.

arguments.third: In the next town, you each teach the other one your game, and then you never mention it again.
lines: sebastian_bloodmage
Football, che, is the only sport where a whole country cries on the same day. Name me another one.
diego_tinker
Baseball, my friend! In Maracaibo the whole street stops for the Aguilas, the whole street, even the dogs.
sebastian_bloodmage
Baseball is a picnic where somebody occasionally runs, boludo. My grandmother could play it in her slippers.

arguments.third: Sebastian does the meat, Yiannis does everything else, and you both sit down to eat it.
lines: yiannis_paladin
Tonight I cook, my friend, a proper Cretan supper, slow, with oil and lemon and patience.
sebastian_bloodmage
Patience is for people who aren't hungry, che. I've already got the fire going and the meat salted.
yiannis_paladin
You salted it already? Panagia mou, without asking the old man, at his own fire on his own beach?

arguments.third: Whoever loses an arm wrestle has to sit through the other one's game and cheer.
lines: sebastian_bloodmage
Football is art, che, twenty two people and one ball and the whole world holding its breath.
rhodri_knight
Football's twenty two lads falling over when the wind blows, butt. Rugby's where you find out who you are.
sebastian_bloodmage
Rugby is a fight in the mud that somebody decided to write rules for afterwards, boludo.

arguments.third: Diego rigs it, Rhodri checks it, and nobody at all stands in front of that door.
lines: diego_tinker
She's ready, my friends, the charge is on the hinge, everybody step back and I light it, yes?
rhodri_knight
No, hang on, mun, you haven't checked the wire, I watched you twist it with your teeth.
diego_tinker
My teeth are very precise, my friend, they've done more wiring than your whole crew put together!

arguments.third: A small fire out here tonight, and the biggest fire in the next town, I promise.
lines: sebastian_bloodmage
More wood, chicos, more wood! A big fire, a proper one, so the meat cooks right and the cold stays out.
sondre_stormbringer
The wind is going to back round before midnight, and a big fire in a backing wind is how you lose a camp.
sebastian_bloodmage
Che, the fire and I have an understanding, we've been friends since before you were born.

sides.diego_tinker: one little spark for the machine

arguments.third: Try it once, in open ground, with everybody standing well back and Sondre calling it.
lines: diego_tinker
Just one spark, my friend, one tiny little lightning into this coil, and she runs for a week!
sondre_stormbringer
No, I am sorry, there is no such thing as one tiny lightning. You are standing right next to the coil.
diego_tinker
So I stand a bit further away! Come on, you're always so careful, it's a coil, not a barn.
sondre_stormbringer
Please do not say that word to me, not about this.

arguments.third: Rhodri holds the front, Sondre goes wide on the flank where there's nobody to hit.
lines: rhodri_knight
I'm stood in front, butt, that's where I go, that's what I'm for, end of discussion.
sondre_stormbringer
If you stand in front, you stand where my storm lands, and I will have to hold it back for you.
rhodri_knight
Then hold it back, mun, I'm not moving, I've had bigger things than weather land on me.

sides.diego_tinker: put a motor on the boat

arguments.third: Diego builds a motor, Yiannis keeps the oars, and the boat gets both.
lines: diego_tinker
Your boat, my friend, imagine it with a little clockwork motor, you'd be at the reef before breakfast!
yiannis_paladin
Before breakfast, you say? Re, the whole point of the morning is the rowing, slow, with the sea waking up around you.
diego_tinker
The sea can wake up faster, it won't mind, I'll make the motor quiet, almost quiet.

arguments.third: Tomorrow morning, one boat: Sondre sails it and Yiannis fishes from it.
lines: sondre_stormbringer
With respect, you only know the top of the water from a fishing boat. Sailing, you have to read all of it.
yiannis_paladin
Only the top of it? Little one, I have been under that water since I was nine, holding my breath for octopus.
sondre_stormbringer
Under it, yes, but a sailor has to argue with the wind as well, and the wind always argues back.

arguments.third: A duet, and whoever forgets the words first does the washing up.
lines: rhodri_knight
Right, song time, boys, and tonight it's Calon Lan, proper, in four parts if you lot can manage two.
yiannis_paladin
Ela, every night the Welsh hymns, my friend. Tonight a mantinada, and I will make one about your beard.
rhodri_knight
My beard is a national treasure, butt, you leave it out of your poetry.

sides.ryan_warlock: a whiskey, neat, after a day like that

arguments.third: You each pour the other a glass of yours, and judge it honestly, on the record.
lines: ryan_warlock
A man finishes a day like that with a whiskey, Esteban, neat, no ice, and no lecture about my liver.
esteban_bloodmage
I'd never lecture you, Ryan. I'd simply note that a carmenere does the same work, with considerably less damage to the stomach lining.
ryan_warlock
The stomach lining, he says. That's the most Chilean way anyone's ever told me to drink wine.

sides.sondre_stormbringer: boil it in the pot with the grounds, like home

arguments.third: Leif makes it his way at dawn, Sondre makes it his way at dusk, and nobody says a word about either.
lines: sondre_stormbringer
Leif, I think perhaps you are making the coffee wrong. In Norway we boil it in the pot, with the grounds, and let them sink.
leif_primalist
Yep, my grandfather did that. Tasted like the bottom of a stump every single morning of my childhood.
sondre_stormbringer
That is the correct taste. Uff, I cannot believe a Halvorsen is saying this to me.

sides.marcus_stormbringer: trust three weeks of pressure readings
sides.sondre_stormbringer: trust the gulls and the water

arguments.third: Marcus keeps his notes, Sondre keeps watch on the beach, and whoever's right gets the first hot drink.
lines: marcus_stormbringer
Sondre, I've got three weeks of pressure readings that say the front comes in tonight, not tomorrow. Three whole weeks of them!
sondre_stormbringer
And I have the gulls, Marcus. They are sitting on the beach, quite calm. A gull does not care about your three weeks.
marcus_stormbringer
You're telling me a seabird is out-forecasting me. Sorry, no, I'm not accepting that, not from a gull.

sides.diego_tinker: put a spring in the lock that pinches whoever picks it
sides.marco_paladin: a lock should be simple and honest

arguments.third: Diego builds his clever lock for the cart, and Marco keeps the inn door simple.
lines: diego_tinker
Marco, my friend, listen, listen, what if your lock had a little spring that pinches the fingers of whoever tries to pick it?
marco_paladin
A lock keeps a door shut, ragazzo. It doesn't bite. Thirty-one years, and none of mine ever bit anyone.
diego_tinker
Sure, sure, and none of yours ever played a little song when it opened either. Think about it, a song, Marco!

sides.yiannis_paladin: light a candle for Saint Nicholas before setting out
sides.ryan_warlock: luck's a deal, and saints don't sign anything

arguments.third: Ryan lights the candle himself, and calls it a gesture of goodwill to the other party.
lines: yiannis_paladin
Ela, Ryan, light a candle with me for Saint Nicholas before we go. He watches over everyone on the water, even brokers.
ryan_warlock
With respect, Yiannis, I've never met a saint who'd sign anything. I'll take my chances with a contract.
yiannis_paladin
A candle is a contract, my boy, the oldest one there is. You give a little light, and he gives you back the shore.

sides.marcus_stormbringer: camp on the ridge, where the sky's in full view
sides.leif_primalist: camp in the hollow, away from that dead snag

arguments.third: Camp in the hollow, and Marcus takes the first watch up on the ridge with his notes.
lines: marcus_stormbringer
The ridge is perfect, Leif, I can see the weather coming for miles, and we'd get a full hour's warning on anything.
leif_primalist
There's a dead snag right over it, leaning at the tents. That wind you're so excited about brings it down at three in the morning.
marcus_stormbringer
So we pitch ten feet to the left of it! I've done the maths, the lean takes it the other way, I'm almost certain.

sides.esteban_bloodmage: ask before you take a single drop, every time
sides.sebastian_bloodmage: it's an ingredient, use what's there

arguments.third: Sebastian asks before he cooks with it, and Esteban stays for dinner.
lines: sebastian_bloodmage
Che, Esteban, a little blood off the boar and a little off the boys, it's all the same in the pan, the fire doesn't ask questions!
esteban_bloodmage
The fire may not, Sebastian. I do, every time, and I'd ask you to start before somebody objects after the fact.
sebastian_bloodmage
After the fact they're eating, boludo, and nobody objects with a full plate. Ask anyone at my table.
